agents.name: Claude Code
agents.context_note: AGENTS.md is read directly from v2.1.277; where it is not available, a CLAUDE.md that imports it covers the same ground.
agents.limits: Project instruction loading is configurable, so which file an agent reads depends on a setting the catalog cannot see.

agents.name: Codex CLI
agents.context_note: Instructions are read from ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, then each AGENTS.md on the way down to the working directory; AGENTS.override.md replaces broader guidance for one subtree.
agents.limits: Project-scoped .codex/config.toml only loads in a trusted directory; the first encounter in an untrusted one prompts before any server starts.

agents.name: GitHub Copilot CLI
agents.context_note: Repository instructions are included automatically for prompts entered in that repository.
agents.limits: Ships with the GitHub MCP server already configured; servers live in ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json. Grant tools individually with --allow-tool rather than --allow-all-tools.

agents.name: Cursor
agents.context_note: A rule file needs YAML frontmatter with description, globs and alwaysApply; a plain .md in .cursor/rules has none and is ignored. Nested AGENTS.md files apply to their own subtree, most specific first.
agents.limits: An editor, not a CLI: setup recipes that assume a terminal agent have to be run by the user. MCP servers are added through the settings UI.

agents.name: Gemini CLI
agents.context_note: The context file name is the `context.fileName` setting and takes a list, so AGENTS.md can be added alongside GEMINI.md rather than replacing it.
agents.limits: Environment variables are expanded in the config with $VAR or ${VAR}, and %VAR% on Windows only.

agents.name: Windsurf
agents.context_note: Rule files carry a `trigger` frontmatter field — always_on, model_decision, glob or manual. A root AGENTS.md has no frontmatter and is always on.
agents.limits: Workspace rule files are capped at 12,000 characters and global ones at 6,000, so a long AGENTS.md is silently truncated. OAuth is unavailable for stdio servers. Documentation now redirects to docs.devin.ai and the config path has moved with it; the legacy path was ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json.

agents.name: Cline
agents.context_note: Reads a workspace AGENTS.md and a cross-tool ~/.agents/AGENTS.md as the standard format for compatibility with other agents.
agents.limits: MCP servers live in ~/.cline/mcp.json for the CLI and in the panel for the extensions. SSE is legacy; use streamableHttp for new servers.

agents.name: OpenCode
agents.context_note: AGENTS.md is preferred and CLAUDE.md is the fallback; the first match wins per category. `instructions` in opencode.json adds more files, and accepts globs and remote URLs.
agents.limits: MCP servers are declared in opencode.json under `mcp` with type local or remote; there is no add subcommand, the file is edited.

agents.name: Kiro
agents.context_note: Steering files use an `inclusion` frontmatter field — always, fileMatch, manual or auto — which must be the first content in the file. An AGENTS.md needs no inclusion mode and is always included.
agents.limits: MCP servers live in .kiro/settings/mcp.json, and an environment variable is only expanded after it is added to the approved-variables setting.

experts.name: Accessibility Specialist
experts.summary: Audit against WCAG 2.2 AA: automated checks first, then the manual passes a scanner cannot make, and every finding names a success criterion and a reproduction.

experts.name: Agent Designer
experts.summary: A workflow before an agent and one agent before several; every tool typed, scoped and able to explain its own errors; and no prompt change without an eval set and a recorded baseline.

experts.name: API Designer
experts.summary: The OpenAPI document is written and linted before the first handler, and every method, status code and error body answers to a named RFC.

experts.name: Code Reviewer
experts.summary: Read the whole diff against its stated intent, run it, and raise only findings that name an input and the wrong result it produces.

experts.name: Debugger
experts.summary: No fix without a committed reproduction, one refutable hypothesis at a time, and a root cause that explains every symptom.

experts.name: DevOps Platform Engineer
experts.summary: Pin by digest, give the build least privilege, make rollback a tested path, and define the SLO before the dashboard.

experts.name: .NET Senior Software Architect
experts.summary: Decide the expensive things first, hold the dependency direction, and refuse the eleven patterns that are structural to remove.

experts.name: Frontend Engineer
experts.summary: Build web UI to targets somebody can measure — WCAG 2.2 AA, Core Web Vitals at the 75th percentile, a declared Baseline and a byte budget — and claim nothing a check did not show.

experts.name: Go Senior Backend Engineer
experts.summary: Build Go services where a context reaches every call, every zero-valued timeout is replaced, errors wrap with %w, and no test ends with a goroutine still running.

experts.name: Go Senior Software Architect
experts.summary: In Go the package is the architecture: keep it small, hide it behind internal/, let consumers own interfaces, and make every goroutine, context and error traceable.

experts.name: Java Senior Backend Engineer
experts.summary: Build Spring Boot services where the JSON mapper rejects what it does not know, @Transactional actually applies, and virtual threads meet a pool sized on purpose.

experts.name: Java Senior Software Architect
experts.summary: Make the module boundaries a failing test, the build bit-for-bit reproducible, the types closed and null-checked, and every Spring proxy do what its annotation claims.

experts.name: Performance Engineer
experts.summary: Measure first, change one thing, measure again — and a result smaller than the run-to-run spread is not a result.

experts.name: PostgreSQL Database Administrator
experts.summary: A backup is a restore somebody ran, an index ships with its plan, and no DDL reaches production without a lock_timeout.

experts.name: Product Manager
experts.summary: The problem before the solution, a metric that could come back negative, criteria somebody could fail, and what is not being built.

experts.name: Python Senior Backend Engineer
experts.summary: Build Python services where pydantic forbids what it was not told about, nothing blocks the event loop, and a session lives exactly as long as one unit of work.

experts.name: QA Automation Lead
experts.summary: Test the behaviour, make it deterministic, treat a flaky test as a failed one, and keep the signal worth acting on.

experts.name: Research Engineer
experts.summary: The question written before the first search, every source graded and dated, every number fetched rather than quoted, disagreements reported instead of settled by taste, and "not found" written down.

experts.name: Security Reviewer
experts.summary: Boundaries first, then authorization. Every finding cites a control at a version, or it is an opinion and stays out.

experts.name: SQL Data Engineer
experts.summary: Model first, migrate in three deploys rather than one, index because a query asked, and assume every load runs twice.

experts.name: Technical Program Manager
experts.summary: Split work across agents only when the plan is wide enough to repay it, freeze the interfaces first, and never let a worker mark its own work done.

experts.name: Technical Writer
experts.summary: Decide the document's type before its first sentence, write for the reader's task, run every sample, and delete more than you add.

experts.name: Test Engineer
experts.summary: Tests inside the code: a failing test before every change, cases derived by a named technique, doubles called what they are, and mutants that prove the assertions bite.

experts.name: TypeScript Senior Backend Engineer
experts.summary: Build Node.js services in TypeScript where every input is parsed, every promise is awaited or handed off on purpose, and every outbound call carries a deadline.

experts.name: TypeScript Senior Software Architect
experts.summary: Let the compiler, the module graph and a schema at every boundary hold the architecture, because in TypeScript a type nothing checks at runtime is a comment.

crews.name: API Hardening Crew
crews.summary: Three specialists for an API that already has users, where the job is finding what is wrong rather than deciding what to build.
crews.for_what: Hardening an API that is already in production: finding the authorization gaps, making the suite worth gating on, and turning a rollback from a belief into a tested path.
crews.not_for: A greenfield project, where there is nothing to harden yet and the decisions worth taking are architectural rather than defensive.

crews.name: SaaS Launch Crew
crews.summary: The four specialists a multi-tenant SaaS needs before its first customer, and the two integrations they all reach for.
crews.for_what: Taking a multi-tenant SaaS from an empty repository to a first paying customer, where the decisions that are expensive to reverse are taken before there is data to migrate.
crews.not_for: A prototype, an internal tool, or anything single-tenant. Four experts on a project with no customers is four opinions nobody has time to reconcile.

integrations.name: Atlassian Rovo MCP Server
integrations.summary: Jira, Confluence, Compass and the rest of Atlassian Cloud through Atlassian's hosted server, as the signed-in user.

install.claude-code: claude mcp add --transport http atlassian https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp
install.codex: codex mcp add atlassian --url https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add --transport http atlassian https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp

integrations.permissions_summary: Reads and writes Jira, Confluence, Compass, Bitbucket and other Atlassian Cloud data with the signed-in user's own permissions: it creates and edits work items and pages, not only reads them.

integrations.name: Azure DevOps MCP Server
integrations.summary: Work items, projects and teams from one Azure DevOps organisation, with the tool domains narrowed to what the work needs.

install.claude-code: claude mcp add --transport stdio azure-devops -- npx -y @azure-devops/mcp@2.10.0 "<your-organization>" -d core work-items
install.codex: codex mcp add azure-devops -- npx -y @azure-devops/mcp@2.10.0 "<your-organization>" -d core work-items
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add azure-devops npx -- -y @azure-devops/mcp@2.10.0 "<your-organization>" -d core work-items

integrations.permissions_summary: Signs in as you and acts with your Azure DevOps permissions in one organisation; with the core and work-items domains it reads projects and work items and can create, update, link and comment on work items.

integrations.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
integrations.summary: Read the console, the network log and a performance trace from a running Chrome, from an agent.

install.codex: codex mcp add chrome-devtools -- npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@1.10.1 --no-usage-statistics
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add chrome-devtools npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@1.10.1 --no-usage-statistics

integrations.permissions_summary: Drives a Chrome instance: navigates, runs JavaScript in its pages, and reads their console, network traffic and performance traces.

integrations.name: Context7
integrations.summary: Library documentation at the version in use, fetched on demand instead of recalled from training.

install.codex: codex mcp add context7 -- npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp@4.1.1
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add context7 npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp@4.1.1

integrations.permissions_summary: Sends the library name and your query to Context7's service and returns documentation.

integrations.name: Exa Search MCP
integrations.summary: Web search built for agents: results as content rather than as a list of links to fetch.

install.codex: codex mcp add exa --env EXA_API_KEY=$EXA_API_KEY -- npx -y exa-mcp-server@3.4.1
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add exa -e EXA_API_KEY=$EXA_API_KEY npx -y exa-mcp-server@3.4.1

integrations.permissions_summary: Sends your search query to Exa's service and returns page content.

integrations.name: Fetch MCP
integrations.summary: Fetch a URL and hand the agent its content as Markdown, including addresses on your own network.

install.codex: codex mcp add fetch -- uvx mcp-server-fetch==2026.8.18
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add fetch uvx mcp-server-fetch==2026.8.18

integrations.permissions_summary: Sends GET requests to any URL the agent asks for, following redirects, from the machine it runs on, including localhost and private network addresses.

integrations.name: Figma Context MCP
integrations.summary: Read a Figma file's layout and styles as structured data, so generated UI matches the design.

install.codex: codex mcp add figma --env FIGMA_API_KEY=$FIGMA_API_KEY -- npx -y figma-developer-mcp@0.13.2 --stdio
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add figma -e FIGMA_API_KEY=$FIGMA_API_KEY npx -y figma-developer-mcp@0.13.2 --stdio

integrations.permissions_summary: Reads the Figma files the access token can reach, through Figma's API.

integrations.name: Filesystem MCP
integrations.summary: Read and write files under directories named on the command line, and nowhere else.

install.codex: codex mcp add filesystem -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem@2026.8.31 /path/to/allowed/dir
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add filesystem npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem@2026.8.31 /path/to/allowed/dir

integrations.permissions_summary: Reads and writes every file under the directories passed as arguments, with the privileges of the user running it.

integrations.name: GitHub MCP Server
integrations.summary: Issues, pull requests, Actions and code search on the repositories a token can reach.

install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add github https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ --transport http --header "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN"

integrations.permissions_summary: Reads and writes every repository the token can reach: issues, pull requests, workflow runs and file contents.

integrations.name: GitLab MCP Server
integrations.summary: GitLab's built-in MCP server (beta): projects, work items, merge requests and pipelines on your own GitLab instance or GitLab.com.

install.claude-code: claude mcp add -s user --transport http GitLab "https://<your-gitlab-host>/api/v4/mcp"
install.codex: codex mcp add GitLab --url "https://<your-gitlab-host>/api/v4/mcp"
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add -t http GitLab "https://<your-gitlab-host>/api/v4/mcp"

integrations.permissions_summary: Signs in as you through OAuth with the mcp scope and acts with your GitLab permissions: reads projects, work items, merge requests and pipelines, and can commit, open and merge merge requests, and run or delete pipelines.

integrations.name: Grafana MCP
integrations.summary: Search dashboards, query Prometheus and Loki, and read alerts and incidents in Grafana, with every write tool switched off.

install.codex: codex mcp add grafana --env "GRAFANA_URL=$GRAFANA_URL" --env "GRAFANA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN=$GRAFANA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN" -- uvx mcp-grafana==1.5.1 --disable-write --usage-stats=disabled
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add grafana -e 'GRAFANA_URL=$GRAFANA_URL' -e 'GRAFANA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN=$GRAFANA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN' uvx mcp-grafana==1.5.1 --disable-write --usage-stats=disabled

integrations.permissions_summary: Reads dashboards, datasources, alert rules, incidents and on-call data, and runs read queries against the datasources, in the Grafana instance the service account can reach; write tools are not registered.

integrations.name: Linear MCP
integrations.summary: Linear issues, projects and comments through Linear's hosted server, read-only unless you choose the full endpoint.

install.claude-code: claude mcp add --transport http linear-server https://mcp.linear.app/mcp/readonly
install.codex: codex mcp add linear --url https://mcp.linear.app/mcp/readonly
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add --transport http linear https://mcp.linear.app/mcp/readonly

integrations.permissions_summary: As installed, reads the issues, projects and comments the signed-in user can see. The full /mcp endpoint, which you opt into, also creates and updates them.

integrations.name: Memory MCP
integrations.summary: A local knowledge graph an agent writes to and reads back across sessions.

install.codex: codex mcp add memory -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory@2026.8.31
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add memory npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory@2026.8.31

integrations.permissions_summary: Reads and writes a knowledge graph in a local file; reaches nothing else.

integrations.name: MongoDB MCP Server
integrations.summary: Query collections, inspect schemas and indexes, and explain plans on a MongoDB deployment, in read-only mode.

install.codex: codex mcp add mongodb --env "MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING=$MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING" -- npx -y mongodb-mcp-server@3.0.4 --readOnly --telemetry disabled
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add mongodb -e 'MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING=$MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING' npx -y mongodb-mcp-server@3.0.4 --readOnly --telemetry disabled

integrations.permissions_summary: Reads every database and collection the connection string's user can read: documents, schemas, indexes, statistics and query plans; create, update and delete tools are not registered.

integrations.name: Next.js DevTools MCP
integrations.summary: Read build and runtime errors, routes and logs from a running Next.js 16+ dev server, and point the agent at the docs for the installed version.

install.codex: codex mcp add next-devtools --env NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 -- npx -y next-devtools-mcp@0.4.0
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add next-devtools -e NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 npx -y next-devtools-mcp@0.4.0

integrations.permissions_summary: Probes local ports for Next.js dev servers and calls the runtime tools they expose at /_next/mcp, which read errors, routes, logs and project metadata; it needs no credentials.

integrations.name: Notion MCP
integrations.summary: Read and write the Notion pages and databases an integration token has been granted.

install.codex: codex mcp add notion --env NOTION_TOKEN=$NOTION_TOKEN -- npx -y @notionhq/notion-mcp-server@2.5.2
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add notion -e NOTION_TOKEN=$NOTION_TOKEN npx -y @notionhq/notion-mcp-server@2.5.2

integrations.permissions_summary: Reads and writes the pages and databases explicitly shared with the integration.

integrations.name: Playwright MCP
integrations.summary: Drive a real browser from an agent: navigate, fill, click and read the accessibility tree.

install.codex: codex mcp add playwright -- npx -y @playwright/mcp@0.0.82
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add playwright npx -y @playwright/mcp@0.0.82

integrations.permissions_summary: Launches a browser on this machine and visits whatever the agent asks it to, including local services.

integrations.name: Sentry MCP
integrations.summary: Read issues, events and stack traces from Sentry, so an agent debugs from the real error.

install.codex: codex mcp add sentry --env SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN=$SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN -- npx -y @sentry/mcp-server@0.40.0
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add sentry -e SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN=$SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN npx -y @sentry/mcp-server@0.40.0

integrations.permissions_summary: Reads issues, events and stack traces, and can update issues (assign, unassign, resolve), in the Sentry organisations the token can reach.

integrations.name: Storybook MCP
integrations.summary: Storybook's official MCP addon: the agent reads your components' docs and stories, previews them and runs their tests from the local dev server.

install.claude-code: npx storybook add @storybook/addon-mcp@10.6.0 && claude mcp add-json storybook '{"type":"http","url":"http://localhost:6006/mcp"}'
install.codex: npx storybook add @storybook/addon-mcp@10.6.0 && codex mcp add storybook --url http://localhost:6006/mcp
install.gemini-cli: npx storybook add @storybook/addon-mcp@10.6.0 && gemini mcp add -t http storybook http://localhost:6006/mcp

integrations.permissions_summary: Serves from your local Storybook dev server with no credentials: reads component docs and stories, runs story tests through Vitest when that addon is installed, and publishes a review of your current changes to its own review page.

integrations.name: Stripe MCP
integrations.summary: The Stripe API and Stripe's documentation through Stripe's hosted server, for the accounts and sandboxes you authorise.

install.claude-code: claude mcp add --transport http stripe https://mcp.stripe.com/
install.codex: codex mcp add stripe --url https://mcp.stripe.com
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add --transport http stripe https://mcp.stripe.com

integrations.permissions_summary: Reads and writes the Stripe accounts and sandboxes you authorise through any Stripe API method, so it moves money: refunds, invoices, subscriptions. Stripe asks a human to confirm refunds and outbound payments.

integrations.name: Supabase MCP Server
integrations.summary: Query one Supabase project's schema, data, logs and docs from an agent, scoped to that project and read-only.

install.claude-code: claude mcp add --scope project --transport http supabase "https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp?read_only=true&project_ref=<your-project-ref>"
install.codex: codex mcp add supabase --url "https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp?read_only=true&project_ref=<your-project-ref>"
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add -t http supabase "https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp?read_only=true&project_ref=<your-project-ref>"

integrations.permissions_summary: Signs in as you through OAuth and, as installed here, reads one project read-only; without read_only it can run SQL that changes data, apply migrations and deploy functions.

integrations.name: Terraform MCP Server
integrations.summary: Look up providers, modules and policies in the public Terraform Registry, so an agent writes HCL against the current schema.

install.codex: codex mcp add terraform -- docker run -i --rm hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server:1.3.0 --toolsets=registry
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add terraform docker run -i --rm hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server:1.3.0 --toolsets=registry

integrations.permissions_summary: Runs a container on this machine that reads public provider, module and policy documentation from the Terraform Registry; with no token set it reaches no workspace, state or run.

integrations.name: Time MCP
integrations.summary: The current time in any IANA time zone, and conversion between zones, so an agent stops guessing the date.

install.codex: codex mcp add time -- uvx mcp-server-time==2026.8.18
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add time uvx mcp-server-time==2026.8.18

integrations.permissions_summary: Reads the system clock and time zone of the machine it runs on and converts times between zones; it reaches no network, file or account.
